intro.data: Here's the seed of the whole finale: you can identify an object purely by the arrows INTO it — its 'fingerprint', Hom(−, X). These three tiers form a ranking (Basic ≤ Plus ≤ Premium), so everything at or below a tier maps into it. Match each tier to the exact set of things that map in. One profile is impossible for a ranking — that's the impostor.
intro.alchemy: The seed of the finale: identify a material purely by the processes INTO it — its fingerprint, Hom(−, X). These three grades form a ranking (Lead ≤ Silver ≤ Gold), so everything at or below maps in. Match each grade to what maps in. One profile is impossible — the impostor.
intro.spellcraft: The seed of the finale: identify an essence purely by the workings INTO it — its fingerprint, Hom(−, X). These three ranks form a ranking (Apprentice ≤ Adept ≤ Archmage), so everything at or below maps in. Match each rank to what maps in. One profile is impossible — the impostor.
intro.abstract: In the chain A ≤ B ≤ C, the representable Hom(−, X) is the set of arrows into X. Match each object to its Hom(−, X). One offered profile is not realizable in a chain (the distractor).

goal.data: Match each tier to the set of tiers that map into it.
goal.alchemy: Match each grade to the set of grades that map into it.
goal.spellcraft: Match each rank to the set of ranks that map into it.
goal.abstract: Pair each object X with its Hom(−, X).

context.data: Hom(−, X) = every arrow into X. In a ranking, that's everything at or below X.
context.alchemy: Hom(−, X) = every process into X — everything at or below X.
context.spellcraft: Hom(−, X) = every working into X — everything at or below X.
context.abstract: Hom(−, X) : the set of arrows into X.

rightLabel.data: What maps into it — Hom(−, X)

label.data: The top maps in, but not the bottom
label.alchemy: The top maps in, but not the bottom
label.spellcraft: The top maps in, but not the bottom

afterSuccess.data: You told the three tiers apart using nothing but the arrows into them. Premium is exactly 'the thing everything maps into'; Basic is 'the thing only it maps into'. That profile — Hom(−, X), every arrow into X — is the REPRESENTABLE functor of X, and it pins the object down completely. The impossible profile had no object, because no object in a ranking has it.
afterSuccess.alchemy: You told the grades apart using only the processes into them. That profile — Hom(−, X) — is the representable functor of X, and it pins the grade down completely.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: You told the ranks apart using only the workings into them. That profile — Hom(−, X) — is the representable functor of X, and it pins the rank down completely.
afterSuccess.abstract: Each object X is identified by Hom(−, X), its representable functor. Distinct objects in the chain have distinct hom-sets-of-incoming-arrows; the non-realizable profile names no object.

reveal.summary: The representable functor Hom(−, X) records every arrow into X — an object's complete fingerprint. An object is known by the arrows into it; that is the idea the Yoneda lemma makes exact.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: A value identified by everything that can produce it — its full set of constructors.
